articles.title: EU endorses Global Electrification Pledge at COP31
articles.summary_excerpt: The European Union has endorsed the 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge at the UN Climate Change Conference COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.

articles.title: Energy Department Announces $2.8 Billion Loan to Strengthen Grid Reliability and Help Lower Costs in Wyoming
articles.summary_excerpt: The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing today announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $2.8 billion for Grid United’s Wyoming Intertie project to lower electricity costs and strengthen grid reliability in Wyoming

articles.title: How does EIA account for small differences between energy supply and demand data?
articles.summary_excerpt: EIA uses over 60 surveys to collect data on the U.S. energy sector's supply and demand. In theory, supply and demand should balance. In practice, we often have small differences between our total supply and total demand figures.

articles.title: In focus: Industrial carbon management – how it works and why we need it
articles.summary_excerpt: Industrial carbon management is not a replacement for clean energy technologies. Rather, it offers solutions complementary to their rollout, and needed for the EU to become the world’s first climate-neutral continent by 2050.

articles.title: Commission approves amended German State aid schemes for energy-intensive companies
articles.summary_excerpt: The European Commission has approved, under EU State aid rules, Germany's amended schemes to compensate energy-intensive companies for indirect emission costs under the EU Emission Trading System (EU ETS) and for temporary electricity price relief under the CISAF and METSAF.

articles.title: Commission approves €9.5 billion Dutch State aid to support offshore wind energy
articles.summary_excerpt: The European Commission has approved, under EU State aid rules, a €9.5 billion Dutch scheme to support renewable electricity production from two offshore wind farms in the North Sea.
